chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Russell Procope and Edgar Sampson in Henderson's band
summary: Jackson met Procope and violinist and composer Edgar Sampson in Henderson's band in 1932; Sampson wrote Stompin' at the Savoy and Blue Lou.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, what about -- when did you run into Russell Procope, just to mention a few of these big names?
I didn't run into Russell Procope until I came to New York.
Uh-huh, and what year was that?
That was 1932. I didn't run into him till then.
Who was he playing with?
He was playing with Fletcher. He was playing with Fletcher then. And a great violinist, too, was playing with Fletcher then, Edgar Sampson. He was in Fletcher's band when I first came to New York.
Edgar Sampson was a great violinist?
Yeah, sure. He made --
I didn't know that.
-- some records with Chick Webb playing
actually, Fletcher Henderson!
violin years ago.
Did he play any other instruments?

He played -- he was a saxophone player and a clarinet player, and a beautiful saxophone player and a good writer. You know, he wrote about three hit tunes that fast. He wrote 'Stompin' at the Savoy' and 'Blue Lou'.
Oh, is that his?
Sure, yes.
And what else?
'Blue Lou' and -- what is that other thing? Da-da da-da de-de-de-da --
That's 'Blue Lou'.
That's 'Blue Lou'?
That's 'Blue Lou'.
Yes, but there's another one that he wrote, too. I can't think of it immediately.
Oh, that's all right.
But a very good arranger.
But most people didn't know that he played the violin.
Oh, yes.
He recorded with -- That's most interesting.
Yeah, he was with Chick Webb, too, you see.
